treatment.logline: A returned phone opens a modest roadside romance, until the same phone brings Anudi's family obligations into the space between them.

arc.beat: A simple return becomes reciprocal curiosity.
Kasun's ambition earns a quiet moment of admiration.
The phone interrupts and the private demand changes Anudi's face.

treatment.approach: Grounded Sri Lankan romantic drama, not suspense: believable rainy roadside light, restrained performances and patient shared frames. Begin with the practical return and gratitude in one shared frame, let the business remain visible during the conversation, and isolate Anudi only when the call displaces their shared attention. The script's actions and dialogue already occupy about 49 seconds; essential handles and cuts raise the must bin above the nominal target.

editor_notes: The 67-second must bin is raw source, not a 67-second required edit. The page itself times at 49 seconds before take handles; the 67.5-second cap leaves only 0.5 seconds for any later pass, so use the existing material rather than assuming room for additional generated takes.
Cut by script block order, not by slate numbering: 4A-1 covers b0–b2; 4A-2 covers b3–b4; 4B-1 covers b5; 4A-3 covers b6–b7. The remainder follows the planned moments.

4A-1 establishes the phone handover and both complete parts of gratitude in one shared frame. The receiving hand and the release must be visibly separated, with no body contact; if the model tangles the hands, use the established beginning and end positions and cut around the transfer.

Use the two-shots for reciprocity and readable business geography; singles for the first business question and the later farewells; the phone insert establishes the incoming source and exact caller ID before any incoming voice; the reaction views keep the caller off screen.

Lay L13–L15 in as phone audio over the silent reaction sources, in order, with the MCU-to-CU cut on a sentence pause. The timing table totals 6.4 seconds for these parts, while the parent-line note says 9.5 seconds; verify the original audio and its sentence pauses before locking the edit, without changing or trimming a line.

The minimum handle fields on several tightly budgeted clips are conservative metadata; their beat windows specify the actual longer settled picture before and after the performance. Protect those visible leads and tails in conform.

Match the phone from Kasun's right hand to Anudi's right hand, then the right ear and finally right hand below her face; keep the open umbrella in her left hand and the handbag on her left shoulder. Use the axis and screen directions throughout.

The first shared position is chosen to continue the preceding scene: Kasun extends the phone from screen right, Anudi receives it on screen left. The state ledger's conflicting initial phone possession is resolved by the scripted handover.
The final wide gives Anudi a left-depth path and Kasun a delayed return to the right-background three-wheeler. Avoid implying he heard the private phone content or specifying his thoughts.

No speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is generated in-camera; if post chooses any, work from the clean locked sources. No mirrors, fast finger work, body contact, elaborate device animation, invented crowd or camera transition has been requested.

editor_notes: The 67-second must bin is raw source, not a 67-second required edit. The page itself times at 49 seconds before take handles; the 67.5-second cap leaves only 0.5 seconds for any later pass, so use the existing material rather than assuming room for additional generated takes.
Cut by script block order, not by slate numbering: 4A-1 covers b0–b2; 4A-2 covers b3–b4; 4B-1 covers b5; 4A-3 covers b6–b7. The remainder follows the planned moments.

4A-1 establishes the phone handover and both complete parts of gratitude in one shared frame. The receiving hand and the release must be visibly separated, with no body contact; if the model tangles the hands, use the established beginning and end positions and cut around the transfer.

Use the two-shots for reciprocity and readable business geography; singles for the first business question and the later farewells; the phone insert establishes the incoming source and exact caller ID before any incoming voice; the reaction views keep the caller off screen.

Lay L13–L15 in as phone audio over the silent reaction sources, in order, with the MCU-to-CU cut on a sentence pause. The timing table totals 6.4 seconds for these parts, while the parent-line note says 9.5 seconds; verify the original audio and its sentence pauses before locking the edit, without changing or trimming a line.

The minimum handle fields on several tightly budgeted clips are conservative metadata; their beat windows specify the actual longer settled picture before and after the performance. Protect those visible leads and tails in conform.

Match the phone from Kasun's right hand to Anudi's right hand, then the right ear and finally right hand below her face; keep the open umbrella in her left hand and the handbag on her left shoulder. Use the axis and screen directions throughout.

The first shared position is chosen to continue the preceding scene: Kasun extends the phone from screen right, Anudi receives it on screen left. The state ledger's conflicting initial phone possession is resolved by the scripted handover.
The final wide gives Anudi a left-depth path and Kasun a delayed return to the right-background three-wheeler. Avoid implying he heard the private phone content or specifying his thoughts.

No speed ramp, freeze frame, digital punch-in or split screen is generated in-camera; if post chooses any, work from the clean locked sources. No mirrors, fast finger work, body contact, elaborate device animation, invented crowd or camera transition has been requested.
